units.leftText: “For there is no good tree that produces rotten fruit, nor again a rotten tree that produces good fruit.

units.rightText: For I myself am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I tell one to go, and he goes, and another to come, and he comes. I tell my servant to do something, and he does it.”

units.leftText: Soon afterwards, he went to a city called Nain. Many of his disciples, along with a great multitude, went with him.

units.rightText: And the dead man sat up and began to speak! Then Jesus gave him back to his mother.

units.leftText: Fear took hold of all, and they glorified God, saying, “A great prophet has arisen among us!” and, “God has visited his people!”
units.rightText: A sense of awe swept over all of them, and they glorified God. “A great prophet has appeared among us!” they said. “God has visited His people!”

units.rightText: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that were performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

units.leftText: But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
units.rightText: But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.

units.leftText: You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, will be brought down to Hades.
units.rightText: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!
leftNotes: 10:15 Hades is the lower realm of the dead, or Hell.

units.leftText: Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. Whoever rejects me rejects him who sent me.”
units.rightText: Whoever listens to you listens to Me; whoever rejects you rejects Me; and whoever rejects Me rejects the One who sent Me.”

units.leftText: The seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!”
units.rightText: The seventy-two returned with joy and said, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in Your name.”

units.leftText: He said to them, “I saw Satan having fallen like lightning from heaven.
units.rightText: So He told them, “I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.

units.leftText: Behold, I give you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will in any way hurt you.
units.rightText: Behold, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. Nothing will harm you.

units.leftText: Nevertheless, don’t rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”
units.rightText: Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”

units.leftText: In that same hour, Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit, and said, “I thank you, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for so it was well-pleasing in your sight.”
units.rightText: At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and declared, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this was well-pleasing in Your sight.

units.leftText: Turning to the disciples, he said, “All things have been delivered to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is, except the Father, and who the Father is, except the Son, and he to whomever the Son desires to reveal him.”
units.rightText: All things have been entrusted to Me by My Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, and no one knows who the Father is except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal Him.”

units.leftText: Turning to the disciples, he said privately, “Blessed are the eyes which see the things that you see,
units.rightText: Then Jesus turned to the disciples and said privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see.

units.leftText: for I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see the things which you see, and didn’t see them, and to hear the things which you hear, and didn’t hear them.”
units.rightText: For I tell you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.”

units.leftText: Behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
units.rightText: One day an expert in the law stood up to test Him. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

units.leftText: He said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
units.rightText: “What is written in the Law?” Jesus replied. “How do you read it?”

units.leftText: He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind; and your neighbor as yourself.”
units.rightText: He answered, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’ and ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ ”
rightNotes: 10:27 Deuteronomy 6:5|DEU 6:5*
10:27 Leviticus 19:18|LEV 19:18*

units.leftText: He said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
units.rightText: “You have answered correctly,” Jesus said. “Do this and you will live.”

units.leftText: But he, desiring to justify himself, asked Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”
units.rightText: But wanting to justify himself, he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?”

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
units.rightText: Jesus took up this question and said, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half dead.

units.leftText: By chance a certain priest was going down that way. When he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
units.rightText: Now by chance a priest was going down the same road, but when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

units.leftText: In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.
units.rightText: So too, when a Levite came to that spot and saw him, he passed by on the other side.

units.leftText: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,
units.rightText: But a Samaritan on a journey came upon him, and when he saw him, he had compassion.

units.leftText: came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
units.rightText: He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

units.leftText: On the next day, when he departed, he took out two denarii, gave them to the host, and said to him, ‘Take care of him. Whatever you spend beyond that, I will repay you when I return.’
units.rightText: The next day he took out two denarii and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Take care of him,’ he said, ‘and on my return I will repay you for any additional expense.’
rightNotes: 10:35 A denarius was customarily a day’s wage for a laborer; see Matthew 20:2|MAT 20:2*.

units.leftText: Now which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?”
units.rightText: Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”

units.leftText: He said, “He who showed mercy on him.”
units.rightText: “The one who showed him mercy,” replied the expert in the law.

units.leftText: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
units.rightText: As they traveled along, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed Him into her home.

units.leftText: She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet and heard his word.
units.rightText: She had a sister named Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message.

units.leftText: But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.”
units.rightText: But Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made. She came to Jesus and said, “Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me!”

units.leftText: Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
units.rightText: “Martha, Martha,” the Lord replied, “you are worried and upset about many things.

units.leftText: but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”
units.rightText: But only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her.”

units.leftText: When he finished praying in a certain place, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples.”
units.rightText: One day in a place where Jesus had just finished praying, one of His disciples requested, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”

units.leftText: He said to them, “When you pray, say,
units.rightText: So Jesus told them, “When you pray, say:

units.leftText: Give us day by day our daily bread.
units.rightText: Give us each day our daily bread.

units.leftText: Forgive us our sins,
units.rightText: And forgive us our sins,

units.leftText: He said to them, “Which of you, if you go to a friend at midnight and tell him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to them, “Suppose one of you goes to his friend at midnight and says, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,

units.leftText: for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him,’
units.rightText: because a friend of mine has come to me on a journey, and I have nothing to set before him.’

units.leftText: and he from within will answer and say, ‘Don’t bother me. The door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed. I can’t get up and give it to you’?
units.rightText: And suppose the one inside answers, ‘Do not bother me. My door is already shut, and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up to give you anything.’

units.leftText: I tell you, although he will not rise and give it to him because he is his friend, yet because of his persistence, he will get up and give him as many as he needs.
units.rightText: I tell you, even though he will not get up to provide for him because of his friendship, yet because of the man’s persistence, he will get up and give him as much as he needs.

units.leftText: “I tell you, keep asking, and it will be given you. Keep seeking, and you will find. Keep knocking, and it will be opened to you.
units.rightText: So I tell you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.

units.leftText: For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
units.rightText: For everyone who asks receives; he who seeks finds; and to him who knocks, the door will be opened.

units.leftText: “Which of you fathers, if your son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, he won’t give him a snake instead of a fish, will he?
units.rightText: What father among you, if his son asks for a fish, will give him a snake instead?
rightNotes: 11:11 BYZ and TR if his son asks for bread, will give him a stone, or for a fish; see Matthew 7:9–10|MAT 7:9-10*.

units.leftText: Or if he asks for an egg, he won’t give him a scorpion, will he?
units.rightText: Or if he asks for an egg, will give him a scorpion?

units.leftText: If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him?”
units.rightText: So if you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!”

units.leftText: He was casting out a demon, and it was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man spoke; and the multitudes marveled.
units.rightText: One day Jesus was driving out a demon that was mute. And when the demon was gone, the man who had been mute spoke. The crowds were amazed,

units.leftText: But some of them said, “He casts out demons by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons.”
units.rightText: but some of them said, “It is by Beelzebul, the prince of the demons, that He drives out demons.”
rightNotes: 11:15 WH Beezeboul; Vulgate Beelzebub; also in verses 18 and 19

units.leftText: Others, testing him, sought from him a sign from heaven.
units.rightText: And others tested Him by demanding a sign from heaven.

units.leftText: But he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. A house divided against itself falls.
units.rightText: Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste, and a house divided against a house will fall.

units.leftText: If Satan also is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
units.rightText: If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? After all, you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.

units.leftText: But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your children cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
units.rightText: And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? So then, they will be your judges.

units.leftText: But if I by God’s finger cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you.
units.rightText: But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

units.leftText: “When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own dwelling, his goods are safe.
units.rightText: When a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure.

units.leftText: But when someone stronger attacks him and overcomes him, he takes from him his whole armor in which he trusted, and divides his plunder.
units.rightText: But when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him, he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder.

units.leftText: “He who is not with me is against me. He who doesn’t gather with me scatters.
units.rightText: He who is not with Me is against Me, and he who does not gather with Me scatters.

units.leftText: The unclean spirit, when he has gone out of the man, passes through dry places, seeking rest; and finding none, he says, ‘I will turn back to my house from which I came out.’
units.rightText: When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through arid places seeking rest and does not find it. Then it says, ‘I will return to the house I left.’

units.leftText: When he returns, he finds it swept and put in order.
units.rightText: On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order.

units.leftText: Then he goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than himself, and they enter in and dwell there. The last state of that man becomes worse than the first.”
units.rightText: Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they go in and dwell there. And the final plight of that man is worse than the first.”

units.leftText: It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!”
units.rightText: As Jesus was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said, “Blessed is the womb that bore You, and blessed are the breasts that nursed You!”

units.leftText: But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”
units.rightText: But He replied, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it.”

units.leftText: When the multitudes were gathering together to him, he began to say, “This is an evil generation. It seeks after a sign. No sign will be given to it but the sign of Jonah the prophet.
units.rightText: As the crowds were increasing, Jesus said, “This is a wicked generation. It demands a sign, but none will be given it except the sign of Jonah.

units.leftText: For even as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will also be to this generation.
units.rightText: For as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.

units.leftText: The Queen of the South will rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, one greater than Solomon is here.
units.rightText: The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and now One greater than Solomon is here.

units.leftText: The men of Nineveh will stand up in the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, one greater than Jonah is here.
units.rightText: The men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and now One greater than Jonah is here.

units.leftText: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, puts it in a cellar or under a basket, but on a stand, that those who come in may see the light.
units.rightText: No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket. Instead, he sets it on a stand, so those who enter can see the light.

units.leftText: The lamp of the body is the eye. Therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is also full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
units.rightText: Your eye is the lamp of your body. When your eyes are good, your whole body also is full of light. But when they are bad, your body is full of darkness.
rightNotes: 11:34 Literally When your eye is sound; see Proverbs 22:9|PRO 22:9*.
11:34 Literally when it is evil; see Proverbs 23:6|PRO 23:6* and Proverbs 28:22.

units.leftText: Therefore see whether the light that is in you isn’t darkness.
units.rightText: Be careful, then, that the light within you is not darkness.

units.leftText: If therefore your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it will be wholly full of light, as when the lamp with its bright shining gives you light.”
units.rightText: So if your whole body is full of light, with no part of it in darkness, you will be radiant, as though a lamp were shining on you.”

units.leftText: Now as he spoke, a certain Pharisee asked him to dine with him. He went in and sat at the table.
units.rightText: As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee invited Him to dine with him; so He went in and reclined at the table.

units.leftText: When the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that he had not first washed himself before dinner.
units.rightText: But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before the meal.

units.leftText: The Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and of the platter, but your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
units.rightText: Then the Lord said, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, but inside you are full of greed and wickedness.

units.leftText: You foolish ones, didn’t he who made the outside make the inside also?
units.rightText: You fools! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside as well?

units.leftText: But give for gifts to the needy those things which are within, and behold, all things will be clean to you.
units.rightText: But give as alms the things that are within you, and behold, everything will be clean for you.

units.leftText: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every herb, but you bypass justice and God’s love. You ought to have done these, and not to have left the other undone.
units.rightText: Woe to you Pharisees! For you pay tithes of mint, rue, and every herb, but you disregard justice and the love of God. You should have practiced the latter without neglecting the former.

units.leftText: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the best seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.
units.rightText: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces.

units.leftText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like hidden graves, and the men who walk over them don’t know it.”
units.rightText: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, which men walk over without even noticing.”

units.leftText: One of the lawyers answered him, “Teacher, in saying this you insult us also.”
units.rightText: One of the experts in the law told Him, “Teacher, when You say these things, You insult us as well.”

units.leftText: He said, “Woe to you lawyers also! For you load men with burdens that are difficult to carry, and you yourselves won’t even lift one finger to help carry those burdens.
units.rightText: “Woe to you as well, experts in the law!” He replied. “For you weigh men down with heavy burdens, but you yourselves will not lift a finger to lighten their load.

units.leftText: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, and your fathers killed them.
units.rightText: Woe to you! For you build tombs for the prophets, but it was your fathers who killed them.

units.leftText: So you testify and consent to the works of your fathers. For they killed them, and you build their tombs.
units.rightText: So you are witnesses consenting to the deeds of your fathers: They killed the prophets, and you build their tombs.

units.leftText: Therefore also the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send to them prophets and apostles; and some of them they will kill and persecute,
units.rightText: Because of this, the wisdom of God said, ‘I will send them prophets and apostles; some of them they will kill and others they will persecute.’

units.leftText: that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
units.rightText: As a result, this generation will be charged with the blood of all the prophets that has been shed since the foundation of the world,

units.leftText: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zachariah, who perished between the altar and the sanctuary.’ Yes, I tell you, it will be required of this generation.
units.rightText: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who was killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, all of it will be charged to this generation.
