units.leftText: Woe to you lawyers! For you took away the key of knowledge. You didn’t enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in, you hindered.”
units.rightText: Woe to you experts in the law! For you have taken away the key to knowledge. You yourselves have not entered, and you have hindered those who were entering.”

units.leftText: As he said these things to them, the scribes and the Pharisees began to be terribly angry, and to draw many things out of him,
units.rightText: As Jesus went on from there, the scribes and Pharisees began to oppose Him bitterly and to ply Him with questions about many things,

units.leftText: lying in wait for him, and seeking to catch him in something he might say, that they might accuse him.
units.rightText: waiting to catch Him in something He might say.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, when a multitude of many thousands had gathered together, so much so that they trampled on each other, he began to tell his disciples first of all, “Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
units.rightText: In the meantime, a crowd of many thousands had gathered, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to speak first to His disciples: “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.

units.leftText: But there is nothing covered up that will not be revealed, nor hidden that will not be known.
units.rightText: There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.

units.leftText: Therefore whatever you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light. What you have spoken in the ear in the inner rooms will be proclaimed on the housetops.
units.rightText: What you have spoken in the dark will be heard in the daylight, and what you have whispered in the inner rooms will be proclaimed from the housetops.

units.leftText: “I tell you, my friends, don’t be afraid of those who kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do.
units.rightText: I tell you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body and after that can do no more.

units.leftText: But I will warn you whom you should fear. Fear him who after he has killed, has power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
units.rightText: But I will show you whom you should fear: Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell. Yes, I tell you, fear Him!
rightNotes: 12:5 Greek Gehenna

units.leftText: “Aren’t five sparrows sold for two assaria coins ? Not one of them is forgotten by God.
units.rightText: Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten by God.
leftNotes: 12:6 An assarion was a small copper coin worth about an hour’s wages for an agricultural laborer.
rightNotes: 12:6 Greek two assaria; an assarion was a Roman copper coin worth about 1/16 of a denarius.

units.leftText: But the very hairs of your head are all counted. Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.
units.rightText: And even the very hairs of your head are all numbered. So do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.

units.leftText: “I tell you, everyone who confesses me before men, the Son of Man will also confess before the angels of God;
units.rightText: I tell you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man will also confess him before the angels of God.

units.leftText: but he who denies me in the presence of men will be denied in the presence of God’s angels.
units.rightText: But whoever denies Me before men will be denied before the angels of God.

units.leftText: Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but those who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
units.rightText: And everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.

units.leftText: When they bring you before the synagogues, the rulers, and the authorities, don’t be anxious how or what you will answer or what you will say;
units.rightText: When you are brought before synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.

units.leftText: for the Holy Spirit will teach you in that same hour what you must say.”
units.rightText: For at that time the Holy Spirit will teach you what you should say.”

units.leftText: One of the multitude said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”
units.rightText: Someone in the crowd said to Him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me.”

units.leftText: But he said to him, “Man, who made me a judge or an arbitrator over you?”
units.rightText: But Jesus replied, “Man, who appointed Me judge or executor between you?”

units.leftText: He said to them, “Beware! Keep yourselves from covetousness, for a man’s life doesn’t consist of the abundance of the things which he possesses.”
units.rightText: And He said to them, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.”

units.leftText: He spoke a parable to them, saying, “The ground of a certain rich man produced abundantly.
units.rightText: Then He told them a parable: “The ground of a certain rich man produced an abundance.

units.leftText: He reasoned within himself, saying, ‘What will I do, because I don’t have room to store my crops?’
units.rightText: So he thought to himself, ‘What shall I do, since I have nowhere to store my crops?’

units.leftText: He said, ‘This is what I will do. I will pull down my barns, build bigger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
units.rightText: Then he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barns and will build bigger ones, and there I will store up all my grain and my goods.

units.leftText: I will tell my soul, “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years. Take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.”’
units.rightText: Then I will say to myself, “You have plenty of good things laid up for many years. Take it easy. Eat, drink, and be merry!”’

units.leftText: “But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’
units.rightText: But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?’

units.leftText: So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”
units.rightText: This is how it will be for anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.”

units.leftText: He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life, what you will eat, nor yet for your body, what you will wear.
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to His disciples, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.

units.leftText: Life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.
units.rightText: For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.

units.leftText: Consider the ravens: they don’t sow, they don’t reap, they have no warehouse or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable are you than birds!
units.rightText: Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storehouse or barn; yet God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!

units.leftText: Which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to his height?
units.rightText: Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?
leftNotes: 12:25 A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters.
rightNotes: 12:25 Or a single cubit to his height; a cubit was approximately 18 inches or 45 centimeters.

units.leftText: If then you aren’t able to do even the least things, why are you anxious about the rest?
units.rightText: So if you cannot do such a small thing, why do you worry about the rest?

units.leftText: Consider the lilies, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin; yet I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
units.rightText: Consider how the lilies grow: They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these.
rightNotes: 12:27 NE and Tischendorf Consider the lilies: They do not spin or weave.

units.leftText: But if this is how God clothes the grass in the field, which today exists and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, O you of little faith?
units.rightText: If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, how much more will He clothe you, O you of little faith!

units.leftText: “Don’t seek what you will eat or what you will drink; neither be anxious.
units.rightText: And do not be concerned about what you will eat or drink. Do not worry about it.

units.leftText: For the nations of the world seek after all of these things, but your Father knows that you need these things.
units.rightText: For the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things, and your Father knows that you need them.

units.leftText: But seek God’s Kingdom, and all these things will be added to you.
units.rightText: But seek His kingdom, and these things will be added unto you.
rightNotes: 12:31 BYZ and TR God’s; see Matthew 6:33|MAT 6:33*.

units.leftText: “Don’t be afraid, little flock, for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the Kingdom.
units.rightText: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father is pleased to give you the kingdom.

units.leftText: Sell what you have and give gifts to the needy. Make for yourselves purses which don’t grow old, a treasure in the heavens that doesn’t fail, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
units.rightText: Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Provide yourselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.

units.leftText: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
units.rightText: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

units.leftText: “Let your waist be dressed and your lamps burning.
units.rightText: Be dressed for service and keep your lamps burning.

units.leftText: Be like men watching for their lord when he returns from the wedding feast, that when he comes and knocks, they may immediately open to him.
units.rightText: Then you will be like servants waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they can open the door for him at once.

units.leftText: Blessed are those servants whom the lord will find watching when he comes. Most certainly I tell you that he will dress himself, make them recline, and will come and serve them.
units.rightText: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds on watch when he returns. Truly I tell you, he will dress himself to serve and will have them recline at the table, and he himself will come and wait on them.

units.leftText: They will be blessed if he comes in the second or third watch and finds them so.
units.rightText: Even if he comes in the second or third watch of the night and finds them alert, those servants will be blessed.
rightNotes: 12:38 That is, between nine at night and three in the morning

units.leftText: But know this, that if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into.
units.rightText: But understand this: If the homeowner had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
rightNotes: 12:39 BYZ and TR include he would have stayed awake, and

units.leftText: Therefore be ready also, for the Son of Man is coming in an hour that you don’t expect him.”
units.rightText: You also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.”

units.leftText: Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or to everybody?”
units.rightText: “Lord,” said Peter, “are You addressing this parable to us, or to everyone else as well?”

units.leftText: The Lord said, “Who then is the faithful and wise steward, whom his lord will set over his household, to give them their portion of food at the right times?
units.rightText: And the Lord answered, “Who then is the faithful and wise manager, whom the master puts in charge of his servants to give them their portion at the proper time?

units.leftText: Blessed is that servant whom his lord will find doing so when he comes.
units.rightText: Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.

units.leftText: Truly I tell you that he will set him over all that he has.
units.rightText: Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.

units.leftText: But if that servant says in his heart, ‘My lord delays his coming,’ and begins to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and to be drunken,
units.rightText: But suppose that servant says in his heart, ‘My master will be a long time in coming,’ and he begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk.

units.leftText: then the lord of that servant will come in a day when he isn’t expecting him and in an hour that he doesn’t know, and will cut him in two, and place his portion with the unfaithful.
units.rightText: The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate. Then he will cut him to pieces and assign him a place with the unbelievers.

units.leftText: That servant who knew his lord’s will, and didn’t prepare nor do what he wanted, will be beaten with many stripes,
units.rightText: That servant who knows his master’s will but does not get ready or follow his instructions will be beaten with many blows.

units.leftText: but he who didn’t know, and did things worthy of stripes, will be beaten with few stripes. To whomever much is given, of him will much be required; and to whom much was entrusted, of him more will be asked.
units.rightText: But the one who unknowingly does things worthy of punishment will be beaten with few blows. From everyone who has been given much, much will be required; and from him who has been entrusted with much, even more will be demanded.

units.leftText: “I came to throw fire on the earth. I wish it were already kindled.
units.rightText: I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!

units.leftText: But I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!
units.rightText: But I have a baptism to undergo, and how distressed I am until it is accomplished!

units.leftText: Do you think that I have come to give peace on the earth? I tell you, no, but rather division.
units.rightText: Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division.

units.leftText: For from now on, there will be five in one house divided, three against two, and two against three.
units.rightText: From now on, five in one household will be divided, three against two and two against three.

units.leftText: They will be divided, father against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against her mother; mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.”
units.rightText: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law. ”
rightNotes: 12:53 See Micah 7:6|MIC 7:6*.

units.leftText: He said to the multitudes also, “When you see a cloud rising from the west, immediately you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and so it happens.
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to the crowds, “As soon as you see a cloud rising in the west, you say, ‘A shower is coming,’ and that is what happens.

units.leftText: When a south wind blows, you say, ‘There will be a scorching heat,’ and it happens.
units.rightText: And when the south wind blows, you say, ‘It will be hot,’ and it is.

units.leftText: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky, but how is it that you don’t interpret this time?
units.rightText: You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and sky. Why don’t you know how to interpret the present time?

units.leftText: “Why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?
units.rightText: And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?

units.leftText: For when you are going with your adversary before the magistrate, try diligently on the way to be released from him, lest perhaps he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
units.rightText: Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate. Otherwise, he may drag you off to the judge, and the judge may hand you over to the officer, and the officer may throw you into prison.

units.leftText: I tell you, you will by no means get out of there until you have paid the very last penny. ”
units.rightText: I tell you, you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny. ”
leftNotes: 12:59 literally, lepton. A lepton is a very small brass Jewish coin worth half a Roman quadrans each, which is worth a quarter of the copper assarion. Lepta are worth less than 1% of an agricultural worker’s daily wages.
rightNotes: 12:59 Greek lepton; that is, a Jewish coin of bronze or copper worth about 1/128 of a denarius

units.leftText: Now there were some present at the same time who told him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
units.rightText: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

units.leftText: Jesus answered them, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?
units.rightText: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this way?

units.leftText: I tell you, no, but unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.
units.rightText: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.

units.leftText: Or those eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you think that they were worse offenders than all the men who dwell in Jerusalem?
units.rightText: Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?

units.leftText: I tell you, no, but, unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.”
units.rightText: No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.”

units.leftText: He spoke this parable. “A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none.
units.rightText: Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it but did not find any.

units.leftText: He said to the vine dresser, ‘Behold, these three years I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, and found none. Cut it down! Why does it waste the soil?’
units.rightText: So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’
rightNotes: 13:7 SBL, NE, WH Cut it down!

units.leftText: He answered, ‘Lord, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
units.rightText: ‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.

units.leftText: If it bears fruit, fine; but if not, after that, you can cut it down.’”
units.rightText: If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’”

units.leftText: He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath day.
units.rightText: One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,

units.leftText: Behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years. She was bent over and could in no way straighten herself up.
units.rightText: and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.

units.leftText: When Jesus saw her, he called her and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your infirmity.”
units.rightText: When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your disability.”

units.leftText: He laid his hands on her, and immediately she stood up straight and glorified God.
units.rightText: Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.

units.leftText: The ruler of the synagogue, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said to the multitude, “There are six days in which men ought to work. Therefore come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day!”
units.rightText: But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. “There are six days for work,” he told the crowd. “So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.”

units.leftText: Therefore the Lord answered him, “You hypocrites! Doesn’t each one of you free his ox or his donkey from the stall on the Sabbath and lead him away to water?
units.rightText: “You hypocrites!” the Lord replied. “Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?

units.leftText: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan had bound eighteen long years, be freed from this bondage on the Sabbath day?”
units.rightText: Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?”

units.leftText: As he said these things, all his adversaries were disappointed; and all the multitude rejoiced for all the glorious things that were done by him.
units.rightText: When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing.

units.leftText: He said, “What is God’s Kingdom like? To what shall I compare it?
units.rightText: Then Jesus asked, “What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?

units.leftText: It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and put in his own garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky live in its branches.”
units.rightText: It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.”

units.leftText: Again he said, “To what shall I compare God’s Kingdom?
units.rightText: Again He asked, “To what can I compare the kingdom of God?

units.leftText: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour, until it was all leavened.”
units.rightText: It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”
leftNotes: 13:21 literally, three sata. 3 sata is about 39 liters or a bit more than a bushel.

units.leftText: He went on his way through cities and villages, teaching, and traveling on to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.

units.leftText: One said to him, “Lord, are they few who are saved?”
units.rightText: “Lord,” someone asked Him, “will only a few people be saved?”

units.leftText: “Strive to enter in by the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter in and will not be able.
units.rightText: “Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.

units.leftText: When once the master of the house has risen up and has shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open to us!’ then he will answer and tell you, ‘I don’t know you or where you come from.’
units.rightText: After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, ‘Lord, open the door for us.’

units.leftText: Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
units.rightText: Then you will say, ‘We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.’

units.leftText: He will say, ‘I tell you, I don’t know where you come from. Depart from me, all you workers of iniquity.’
units.rightText: And he will answer, ‘I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.’

units.leftText: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God’s Kingdom, and yourselves being thrown outside.
units.rightText: There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.

units.leftText: They will come from the east, west, north, and south, and will sit down in God’s Kingdom.
units.rightText: People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Behold, there are some who are last who will be first, and there are some who are first who will be last.”
units.rightText: And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.”

units.leftText: On that same day, some Pharisees came, saying to him, “Get out of here and go away, for Herod wants to kill you.”
units.rightText: At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, “Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.”

units.leftText: He said to them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I complete my mission.
units.rightText: But Jesus replied, “Go tell that fox, ‘Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.’

units.leftText: Nevertheless I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the next day, for it can’t be that a prophet would perish outside of Jerusalem.’
units.rightText: Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.

units.leftText: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to her! How often I wanted to gather your children together, like a hen gathers her own brood under her wings, and you refused!
units.rightText: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!

units.leftText: Behold, your house is left to you desolate. I tell you, you will not see me until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
units.rightText: Look, your house is left to you desolate. And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.’ ”

units.leftText: When he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him.
units.rightText: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.

units.leftText: Behold, a certain man who had dropsy was in front of him.
units.rightText: Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.

units.leftText: Jesus, answering, spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?”
units.rightText: So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”

units.leftText: But they were silent.
units.rightText: But they remained silent.

units.leftText: He answered them, “Which of you, if your son or an ox fell into a well, wouldn’t immediately pull him out on a Sabbath day?”
units.rightText: And He asked them, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”
rightNotes: 14:5 TR donkey

units.leftText: They couldn’t answer him regarding these things.
units.rightText: And they were unable to answer these questions.

units.leftText: He spoke a parable to those who were invited, when he noticed how they chose the best seats, and said to them,
units.rightText: When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable:

units.leftText: “When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, don’t sit in the best seat, since perhaps someone more honorable than you might be invited by him,
units.rightText: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.

units.leftText: and he who invited both of you would come and tell you, ‘Make room for this person.’ Then you would begin, with shame, to take the lowest place.
units.rightText: Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your seat.’ And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.

units.leftText: But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may tell you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all who sit at the table with you.
units.rightText: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.
rightNotes: 14:10 See Proverbs 25:7|PRO 25:7*.

units.leftText: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
units.rightText: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

units.leftText: He also said to the one who had invited him, “When you make a dinner or a supper, don’t call your friends, nor your brothers, nor your kinsmen, nor rich neighbors, or perhaps they might also return the favor, and pay you back.
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.

units.leftText: But when you make a feast, ask the poor, the maimed, the lame, or the blind;
units.rightText: But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,

units.leftText: and you will be blessed, because they don’t have the resources to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.”
units.rightText: and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”

units.leftText: When one of those who sat at the table with him heard these things, he said to him, “Blessed is he who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”
units.rightText: When one of those reclining with Him heard this, he said to Jesus, “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”
rightNotes: 14:15 Literally who will eat bread

units.leftText: But he said to him, “A certain man made a great supper, and he invited many people.
units.rightText: But Jesus replied, “A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.

units.leftText: He sent out his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited, ‘Come, for everything is ready now.’
units.rightText: When it was time for the banquet, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’

units.leftText: They all as one began to make excuses.
units.rightText: But one after another they all began to make excuses. The first one said, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.’

units.leftText: “Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go try them out. Please have me excused.’
units.rightText: Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’

units.leftText: “Another said, ‘I have married a wife, and therefore I can’t come.’
units.rightText: Still another said, ‘I have married a wife, so I cannot come.’

units.leftText: “That servant came, and told his lord these things. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, maimed, blind, and lame.’
units.rightText: The servant returned and reported all this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’

units.leftText: “The servant said, ‘Lord, it is done as you commanded, and there is still room.’
units.rightText: ‘Sir,’ the servant replied, ‘what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.’

units.leftText: “The lord said to the servant, ‘Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
units.rightText: So the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.

units.leftText: For I tell you that none of those men who were invited will taste of my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen. ’”
units.rightText: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.’”
leftNotes: 14:24 RP MT includes the last sentence. TR, NU, and FH MT omit: For many are called, but few are chosen.

units.leftText: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,
units.rightText: Now large crowds were traveling with Jesus, and He turned and said to them,

units.leftText: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.
units.rightText: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters — yes, even his own life — he cannot be My disciple.

units.leftText: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross and come after me, can’t be my disciple.
units.rightText: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.

units.leftText: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?
units.rightText: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?

units.leftText: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation and isn’t able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,
units.rightText: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him,

units.leftText: saying, ‘This man began to build and wasn’t able to finish.’
units.rightText: saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’

units.leftText: Or what king, as he goes to encounter another king in war, will not sit down first and consider whether he is able with ten thousand to meet him who comes against him with twenty thousand?
units.rightText: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?

units.leftText: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sends an envoy and asks for conditions of peace.
units.rightText: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.

units.leftText: So therefore, whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.
units.rightText: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple.

units.leftText: “Salt is good, but if the salt becomes flat and tasteless, with what do you season it?
units.rightText: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned?

units.leftText: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. It is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
units.rightText: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out.

units.leftText: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.
units.rightText: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were gathering around to listen to Jesus.

units.leftText: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”
units.rightText: So the Pharisees and scribes began to grumble: “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”

units.leftText: He told them this parable:
units.rightText: Then Jesus told them this parable:

units.leftText: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?
units.rightText: “What man among you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the pasture and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?

units.leftText: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
units.rightText: And when he finds it, he joyfully puts it on his shoulders,

units.leftText: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’
units.rightText: comes home, and calls together his friends and neighbors to tell them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost sheep!’

units.leftText: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.
units.rightText: I tell you that in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who do not need to repent.

units.leftText: “Or what woman, if she had ten drachma coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?
units.rightText: Or what woman who has ten silver coins and loses one of them does not light a lamp, sweep her house, and search carefully until she finds it?
leftNotes: 15:8 A drachma coin was worth about a days wages for an agricultural laborer.
rightNotes: 15:8 Greek ten drachmas, each worth about a day’s wages

units.leftText: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost!’
units.rightText: And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors to say, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my lost coin.’

units.leftText: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”
units.rightText: In the same way, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”

units.leftText: He said, “A certain man had two sons.
units.rightText: Then Jesus said, “There was a man who had two sons.

units.leftText: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ So he divided his livelihood between them.
units.rightText: The younger son said to him, ‘Father, give me my share of the estate.’ So he divided his property between them.

units.leftText: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.
units.rightText: After a few days, the younger son got everything together and journeyed to a distant country, where he squandered his wealth in wild living.

units.leftText: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.
units.rightText: After he had spent all he had, a severe famine swept through that country, and he began to be in need.

units.leftText: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.
units.rightText: So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.

units.leftText: He wanted to fill his belly with the pods that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.
units.rightText: He longed to fill his belly with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one would give him a thing.

units.leftText: But when he came to himself, he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!
units.rightText: Finally he came to his senses and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired servants have plenty of food, but here I am, starving to death!

units.leftText: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight.
units.rightText: I will get up and go back to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.

units.leftText: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’
units.rightText: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired servants.”’

units.leftText: “He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
units.rightText: So he got up and went to his father. But while he was still in the distance, his father saw him and was filled with compassion. He ran to his son, embraced him, and kissed him.

units.leftText: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’
units.rightText: The son declared, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son. ’
rightNotes: 15:21 WH includes Make me like one of your hired servants; see verse 19.

units.leftText: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
units.rightText: But the father said to his servants, ‘Quick! Bring the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.

units.leftText: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat and celebrate;
units.rightText: Bring the fattened calf and kill it. Let us feast and celebrate.

units.leftText: for this, my son, was dead and is alive again. He was lost and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.
units.rightText: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again! He was lost and is found!’ So they began to celebrate.

units.leftText: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.
units.rightText: Meanwhile the older son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.

units.leftText: He called one of the servants to him and asked what was going on.
units.rightText: So he called one of the servants and asked what was going on.

units.leftText: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’
units.rightText: ‘Your brother has returned,’ he said, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has him back safe and sound.’

units.leftText: But he was angry and would not go in. Therefore his father came out and begged him.
units.rightText: The older son became angry and refused to go in. So his father came out and pleaded with him.

units.leftText: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.
units.rightText: But he answered his father, ‘Look, all these years I have served you and never disobeyed a commandment of yours. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.

units.leftText: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’
units.rightText: But when this son of yours returns from squandering your wealth with prostitutes, you kill the fattened calf for him!’

units.leftText: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
units.rightText: ‘Son, you are always with me,’ the father said, ‘and all that is mine is yours.

units.leftText: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”
units.rightText: But it was fitting to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’”

units.leftText: He also said to his disciples, “There was a certain rich man who had a manager. An accusation was made to him that this man was wasting his possessions.
units.rightText: Jesus also said to His disciples, “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.

units.leftText: He called him, and said to him, ‘What is this that I hear about you? Give an accounting of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’
units.rightText: So he called him in to ask, ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’

units.leftText: “The manager said within himself, ‘What will I do, seeing that my lord is taking away the management position from me? I don’t have strength to dig. I am ashamed to beg.
units.rightText: The manager said to himself, ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg.

units.leftText: I know what I will do, so that when I am removed from management, they may receive me into their houses.’
units.rightText: I know what I will do so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’

units.leftText: Calling each one of his lord’s debtors to him, he said to the first, ‘How much do you owe to my lord?’
units.rightText: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors. ‘How much do you owe my master?’ he asked the first.

units.leftText: He said, ‘A hundred batos of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and sit down quickly and write fifty.’
units.rightText: ‘A hundred measures of olive oil,’ he answered.
leftNotes: 16:6 100 batos is about 395 liters or 104 U. S. gallons.
rightNotes: 16:6 Greek ‘A hundred baths of oil’; that is, approximately 870 gallons or 3,300 liters

units.leftText: Then he said to another, ‘How much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred cors of wheat.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, and write eighty.’
units.rightText: Then he asked another, ‘And how much do you owe?’

units.leftText: “His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.
units.rightText: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.

units.leftText: I tell you, make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when you fail, they may receive you into the eternal tents.
units.rightText: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.

units.leftText: He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
units.rightText: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.

units.leftText: If therefore you have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?
units.rightText: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?

units.leftText: If you have not been faithful in that which is another’s, who will give you that which is your own?
units.rightText: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another, who will give you belongings of your own?

units.leftText: No servant can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will hold to one and despise the other. You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon.”
units.rightText: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and money.”
leftNotes: 16:13 “Mammon” refers to riches or a false god of wealth.

units.leftText: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, also heard all these things, and they scoffed at him.
units.rightText: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.

units.leftText: He said to them, “You are those who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts. For that which is exalted among men is an abomination in the sight of God.
units.rightText: So He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before men, but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.

units.leftText: “The law and the prophets were until John. From that time the Good News of God’s Kingdom is preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
units.rightText: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John. Since that time, the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached, and everyone is forcing his way into it.
rightNotes: 16:16 Or everyone is urged to enter into it

units.leftText: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tiny stroke of a pen in the law to fall.
units.rightText: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.

units.leftText: “Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery. He who marries one who is divorced from a husband commits adultery.
units.rightText: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

units.leftText: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.
units.rightText: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.

units.leftText: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,
units.rightText: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores

units.leftText: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
units.rightText: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs came and licked his sores.

units.leftText: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
units.rightText: One day the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side. And the rich man also died and was buried.
rightNotes: 16:22 Greek into Abraham’s bosom; similarly in verse 23

units.leftText: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.
units.rightText: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.

units.leftText: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’
units.rightText: So he cried out, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue. For I am in agony in this fire.’

units.leftText: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted and you are in anguish.
units.rightText: But Abraham answered, ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.

units.leftText: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’
units.rightText: And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you, nor can anyone cross from there to us.’

units.leftText: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house—
units.rightText: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ he said, ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,

units.leftText: for I have five brothers—that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’
units.rightText: for I have five brothers. Let him warn them, so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’

units.leftText: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’
units.rightText: But Abraham replied, ‘They have Moses and the Prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’

units.leftText: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’
units.rightText: ‘No, father Abraham,’ he said, ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’

units.leftText: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’”
units.rightText: Then Abraham said to him, ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”

units.leftText: He said to the disciples, “It is impossible that no occasions of stumbling should come, but woe to him through whom they come!
units.rightText: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!

units.leftText: It would be better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea, rather than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
units.rightText: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.

units.leftText: Be careful. If your brother sins against you, rebuke him. If he repents, forgive him.
units.rightText: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.

units.leftText: If he sins against you seven times in the day, and seven times returns, saying, ‘I repent,’ you shall forgive him.”
units.rightText: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”

units.leftText: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
units.rightText: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”

units.leftText: The Lord said, “If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would tell this sycamore tree, ‘Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
units.rightText: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.

units.leftText: But who is there among you, having a servant plowing or keeping sheep, that will say when he comes in from the field, ‘Come immediately and sit down at the table’?
units.rightText: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?

units.leftText: Wouldn’t he rather tell him, ‘Prepare my supper, clothe yourself properly, and serve me while I eat and drink. Afterward you shall eat and drink’?
units.rightText: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink, and afterward you may eat and drink’?

units.leftText: Does he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded? I think not.
units.rightText: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?

units.leftText: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”
units.rightText: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”

units.leftText: As he was on his way to Jerusalem, he was passing along the borders of Samaria and Galilee.
units.rightText: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.

units.leftText: As he entered into a certain village, ten men who were lepers met him, who stood at a distance.
units.rightText: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance
rightNotes: 17:12 A leper was one afflicted with a skin disease. See Leviticus 13.

units.leftText: They lifted up their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
units.rightText: and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”

units.leftText: When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
units.rightText: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.
rightNotes: 17:14 See Leviticus 14:1–32|LEV 14:1-32*.

units.leftText: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
units.rightText: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.

units.leftText: He fell on his face at Jesus’ feet, giving him thanks; and he was a Samaritan.
units.rightText: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him — and he was a Samaritan.

units.leftText: Jesus answered, “Weren’t the ten cleansed? But where are the nine?
units.rightText: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?

units.leftText: Were there none found who returned to give glory to God, except this foreigner?”
units.rightText: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”

units.leftText: Then he said to him, “Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well! ”
rightNotes: 17:19 Or has saved you

units.leftText: Being asked by the Pharisees when God’s Kingdom would come, he answered them, “God’s Kingdom doesn’t come with observation;
units.rightText: When asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, Jesus replied, “The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs.

units.leftText: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
units.rightText: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’ For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst. ”
rightNotes: 17:21 Or within you or within your grasp

units.leftText: He said to the disciples, “The days will come when you will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
units.rightText: Then He said to the disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.

units.leftText: They will tell you, ‘Look, here!’ or ‘Look, there!’ Don’t go away or follow after them,
units.rightText: People will tell you, ‘Look, there He is!’ or ‘Look, here He is!’ Do not go out or chase after them.

units.leftText: for as the lightning, when it flashes out of one part under the sky, shines to another part under the sky, so will the Son of Man be in his day.
units.rightText: For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day.

units.leftText: But first, he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
units.rightText: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.

units.leftText: As it was in the days of Noah, even so it will also be in the days of the Son of Man.
units.rightText: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man:

units.leftText: They ate, they drank, they married, and they were given in marriage until the day that Noah entered into the ship, and the flood came and destroyed them all.
units.rightText: People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.

units.leftText: Likewise, even as it was in the days of Lot: they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, they built;
units.rightText: It was the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.

units.leftText: but in the day that Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from the sky and destroyed them all.
units.rightText: But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.

units.leftText: It will be the same way in the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
units.rightText: It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.

units.leftText: In that day, he who will be on the housetop and his goods in the house, let him not go down to take them away. Let him who is in the field likewise not turn back.
units.rightText: On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions. Likewise, let no one in the field return for anything he has left behind.

units.leftText: Remember Lot’s wife!
units.rightText: Remember Lot’s wife!

units.leftText: Whoever seeks to save his life loses it, but whoever loses his life preserves it.
units.rightText: Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it.

units.leftText: I tell you, in that night there will be two people in one bed. One will be taken and the other will be left.
units.rightText: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed: one will be taken and the other left.

units.leftText: There will be two grinding grain together. One will be taken and the other will be left.”
units.rightText: Two women will be grinding grain together: one will be taken and the other left.”
rightNotes: 17:35 TR includes 36*Two men will be in the field. One will be taken and the other left; see Matthew 24:40|MAT 24:40*.

leftNotes: 17:36 Some Greek manuscripts add: “Two will be in the field: the one taken, and the other left.”

units.leftText: They, answering, asked him, “Where, Lord?”
units.rightText: “Where, Lord?” they asked.

units.leftText: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray and not give up,
units.rightText: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart:

units.leftText: saying, “There was a judge in a certain city who didn’t fear God and didn’t respect man.
units.rightText: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.

units.leftText: A widow was in that city, and she often came to him, saying, ‘Defend me from my adversary!’
units.rightText: And there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’

units.leftText: He wouldn’t for a while; but afterward he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect man,
units.rightText: For a while he refused, but later he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect men,

units.leftText: yet because this widow bothers me, I will defend her, or else she will wear me out by her continual coming.’”
units.rightText: yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Otherwise, she will wear me out with her perpetual requests.’”

units.leftText: The Lord said, “Listen to what the unrighteous judge says.
units.rightText: And the Lord said, “Listen to the words of the unjust judge.

units.leftText: Won’t God avenge his chosen ones who are crying out to him day and night, and yet he exercises patience with them?
units.rightText: Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He delay in helping them?

units.leftText: I tell you that he will avenge them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
units.rightText: I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?”

units.leftText: He also spoke this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others:
units.rightText: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable:

units.leftText: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
units.rightText: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.

units.leftText: The Pharisee stood and prayed by himself like this: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of men: extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
units.rightText: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like other men — swindlers, evildoers, adulterers — or even like this tax collector.
rightNotes: 18:11 Or stood and prayed to himself

units.leftText: I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’
units.rightText: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’

units.leftText: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his chest, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
units.rightText: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’

units.leftText: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
units.rightText: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

units.leftText: They were also bringing their babies to him, that he might touch them. But when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
units.rightText: Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.

units.leftText: Jesus summoned them, saying, “Allow the little children to come to me, and don’t hinder them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.
units.rightText: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

units.leftText: Most certainly, I tell you, whoever doesn’t receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”
units.rightText: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”

units.leftText: A certain ruler asked him, saying, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?”
units.rightText: Then a certain ruler asked Him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

units.leftText: Jesus asked him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good, except one: God.
units.rightText: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.

units.leftText: You know the commandments: ‘Don’t commit adultery,’ ‘Don’t murder,’ ‘Don’t steal,’ ‘Don’t give false testimony,’ ‘Honor your father and your mother.’”
units.rightText: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’ ”

units.leftText: He said, “I have observed all these things from my youth up.”
units.rightText: “All these I have kept from my youth,” he said.

units.leftText: When Jesus heard these things, he said to him, “You still lack one thing. Sell all that you have and distribute it to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”
units.rightText: On hearing this, Jesus told him, “You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”

units.leftText: But when he heard these things, he became very sad, for he was very rich.
units.rightText: But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.

units.rightText: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.

units.rightText: While they were puzzling over this, suddenly two men in radiant apparel stood beside them.

units.rightText: As the women bowed their faces to the ground in terror, the two men asked them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?

units.leftText: He isn’t here, but is risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee,
units.rightText: He is not here; He has risen! Remember how He told you while He was still in Galilee:

units.leftText: saying that the Son of Man must be delivered up into the hands of sinful men and be crucified, and the third day rise again?”

units.rightText: It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told this to the apostles.

units.rightText: But their words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.

units.leftText: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. Stooping and looking in, he saw the strips of linen lying by themselves, and he departed to his home, wondering what had happened.
units.rightText: Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. And after bending down and seeing only the linen cloths, he went away, wondering to himself what had happened.

units.leftText: Behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
units.rightText: That same day two of them were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 24:13 60 stadia = about 11 kilometers or about 7 miles.
rightNotes: 24:13 Greek being sixty stadia in distance; that is, approximately 6.9 miles or 11.1 kilometers

units.leftText: They talked with each other about all of these things which had happened.
units.rightText: They were talking with each other about everything that had happened.

units.leftText: While they talked and questioned together, Jesus himself came near, and went with them.
units.rightText: And as they talked and deliberated, Jesus Himself came up and walked along with them.

units.leftText: But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
units.rightText: But their eyes were kept from recognizing Him.

units.rightText: He asked them, “What are you discussing so intently as you walk along?”

units.rightText: One of them, named Cleopas, asked Him, “Are You the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in recent days?”

units.rightText: “What things?” He asked.

units.leftText: and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him up to be condemned to death, and crucified him.

units.rightText: But we were hoping He was the One who would redeem Israel. And besides all this, it is the third day since these things took place.

units.leftText: Also, certain women of our company amazed us, having arrived early at the tomb;
units.rightText: Furthermore, some of our women astounded us. They were at the tomb early this morning,

units.rightText: but they did not find His body. They came and told us they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.

units.leftText: He said to them, “Foolish people, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
units.rightText: Then Jesus said to them, “O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!

units.leftText: Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?”
units.rightText: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then to enter His glory?”

units.leftText: Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.
units.rightText: And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.

units.leftText: They came near to the village where they were going, and he acted like he would go further.
units.rightText: As they approached the village where they were headed, He seemed to be going farther.

units.leftText: They urged him, saying, “Stay with us, for it is almost evening, and the day is almost over.”
units.rightText: But they pleaded with Him, “Stay with us, for it is nearly evening and the day is almost over.”

units.leftText: When he had sat down at the table with them, he took the bread and gave thanks. Breaking it, he gave it to them.
units.rightText: While He was reclining at the table with them, He took bread, spoke a blessing and broke it, and gave it to them.

units.leftText: Their eyes were opened and they recognized him; then he vanished out of their sight.
units.rightText: Then their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus — and He disappeared from their sight.

units.leftText: They said to one another, “Weren’t our hearts burning within us while he spoke to us along the way, and while he opened the Scriptures to us?”
units.rightText: They asked each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us as He spoke with us on the road and opened the Scriptures to us?”

units.leftText: They rose up that very hour, returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and those who were with them,
units.rightText: And they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!”

units.rightText: Then the two told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized Jesus in the breaking of the bread.

units.rightText: While they were describing these events, Jesus Himself stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”

units.leftText: But they were terrified and filled with fear, and supposed that they had seen a spirit.
units.rightText: But they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit.

units.rightText: “Why are you troubled,” Jesus asked, “and why do doubts arise in your hearts?

units.leftText: See my hands and my feet, that it is truly me. Touch me and see, for a spirit doesn’t have flesh and bones, as you see that I have.”
units.rightText: Look at My hands and My feet. It is I Myself. Touch Me and see — for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.”

units.rightText: While they were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement, He asked them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”

units.rightText: So they gave Him a piece of broiled fish,

units.leftText: He took them, and ate in front of them.
units.rightText: and He took it and ate it in front of them.

units.rightText: Jesus said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you while I was still with you: Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms.”

units.leftText: Then he opened their minds, that they might understand the Scriptures.
units.rightText: Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
